newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan utilities seen cutting gas,electricity rates.
newsitem.headline: Japan utilities seen cutting gas,electricity rates.

text.p: Japan's electricity and gas rates are expected to be cut from October due to a decline in the cost of fuels such as liquefied natural gas (LNG), coal and crude oil, power industry sources said on Thursday.
The rates are reviewed every quarter and are calculated based on the import price of fuels the utilities use, under a pricing system introduced in January 1996.
This would be the first cut in rates since the new pricing system was introduced, industry sources said.
Third-quarter rates will be based on the price of fuel during the April-June period. Japan relies on imports for the bulk of its energy needs.
Crude oil and LNG prices were lower during that period than in the January-March period, data from the Federation of Electric Power Companies shows.
Figures for coal were not yet available.
The size of the reduction in electricity rates will depend on the composition of fuel each utility uses.
The federation said eight of Japan's 10 electric power utilities were expected to cut rates by about 10 to 76 yen a month for the average household, according to preliminary calculations.
Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc and Kansai Electric Power Co Inc, however, are expected to keep their rates unchanged, the federation said.
A Tokyo Gas Co Ltd spokesman said that the company expected to cut gas rates from 90 to 95 yen a month from October.

Japan has about 244 gas companies nationwide, but the four top companies -- Tokyo Gas Co Ltd, Osaka Gas Co Ltd, Toho Gas Co Ltd and Saibu Gas Co Ltd -- together supply about 70 percent of the nation's households.
